- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven support.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-period moving average of forecast to reduce noise.
- When true outcome is below 65% of historical mean, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust downward by 3–8% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the period; apply 1–3% downward correction for first 5–7 days if sentiment is weak.
- If sentiment history shows increasing negativity (e.g., 3 consecutive drops), model often fails to anticipate further decline; apply 2–5% downward bias for next 5 days.
